chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: In Duke Ellington's band
summary: Duke features everyone once but favours veterans; McGhee likes the band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Now, getting back to Duke. After Duke went into Basin Street, I couldn't work there, so I was out of the band. I guess I didn't really want to stay with Duke, with that band anyway, because... I enjoyed the band, I loved it. But something wasn't right. I didn't really get the feeling that I belonged in Duke's band.
Were you featured on certain things?

Well, yeah, Duke featured... He features everybody once a night at least. He'd give you a tune to play or one of his songs to play, he'd feature you out in front of the band. But he don't really put you out there, because the only thing he's interested in is the guys that's been with him for years. They're the ones that he wants to get out front, like Johnny Anderson, Cat Anderson, Cootie Williams...
Were they all in the band when you were in the band?
Well, Cootie Williams and Cat Anderson were.
Yeah, Harry Carney was there. He was a beautiful guy.
What kind of a personal contact did you have with Duke?

Duke and I got along very good. In fact, he helped me put the big band together, in a sense. Like, he'd talk to me and tell me what's going on, and how to go about doing certain things. He was very nice to me. Except that he was sorry that I couldn't work at the thing with him, because he would have liked to keep me in the band. But I just couldn't stay. I couldn't lay off and wait until they came out of the club, because I had to make a living. I had to make it on my own if I can't make it with Duke, you know.
So that's what happened with Duke and I. But I had a beautiful relationship with him. In fact, the whole band. I liked the whole band, man. They were very nice; they were very nice to me, too.
